reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea is to model basketball player movement as a stochastic process governed by Markovian dynamics. Each player's position at time t is conditioned solely on their prior position, forming a Markov chain. This simplifies analysis yet retains interpretability. Transition densities are estimated using either parametric forms (e.g., Gaussian errors) or nonparametric methods that adapt to complex spatial structures. The paper extends this to a Poisson point process framework, allowing for scalable modeling of large datasets. The transition density p(x_t|x_{t−1}) is derived from intensity functions λ(x_t, x_{t−1}), which generalize multinomial estimation to continuous domains. This enables robust inference even when data is sparse or irregular. The resulting framework supports both short-term tactical predictions and long-term strategic insights by combining statistical rigor with spatial awareness.
